classification.difficultyReason: Reads roots from factors, uses their midpoint and substitution for the vertex, and sketches; reversed factors require checking the actual leading sign for concavity.

content.prompt: Using the $x$-intercepts, sketch the graphs of the following parabolas. Label the turning point.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+2}{2}\\x&=1\\y&=1(1-2)\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(1,-1)$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives an upward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with arrowed axes, no grid or ticks, two intercepts and the turning point.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}2x(x+2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }-2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-2+0}{2}\\x&=-1\\y&=2(-1)(-1+2)\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-1,-2)$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives an upward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Complete upward-opening solution sketch with labelled roots and turning point; arrowed axes without ticks or grid.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}-x(x-3)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+3}{2}\\x&=\frac32\\y&=-\frac32\left(\frac32-3\right)\\y&=\frac94\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $\left(\frac32,\frac94\right)$. The negative coefficient of $x^2$ gives a downward-opening parabola.

For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}-x(x+4)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }-4\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}x(2-x)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+2}{2}\\x&=1\\y&=1(2-1)\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(1,1)$. Since $x(2-x)=-x^2+2x$, the parabola opens downwards.

spec.description: Complete downward-opening solution sketch with roots and maximum labelled.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}-2x(3-x)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+3}{2}\\x&=\frac32\\y&=-2\left(\frac32\right)\left(3-\frac32\right)\\y&=-\frac92\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $\left(\frac32,-\frac92\right)$. Since $-2x(3-x)=2x^2-6x$, the parabola opens upwards.

spec.description: Complete upward-opening solution sketch, retaining the sign reversal from the factor 3-x and an exact fractional vertex.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)(x-3)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{1+3}{2}\\x&=2\\y&=(2-1)(2-3)\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$,
$$y=(0-1)(0-3)=3.$$
The turning point is $(2,-1)$ and the $y$-intercept is $(0,3)$. The parabola opens upwards.

spec.description: Complete upward-opening solution sketch with both axial intercepts and turning point labelled.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}-(x+1)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-1\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-1+1}{2}\\x&=0\\y&=-(0+1)(0-1)\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(0,1)$, also the $y$-intercept. The negative coefficient of $x^2$ gives a downward-opening parabola.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-2\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-2+1}{2}\\x&=-\frac12\\y&=\left(-\frac12+2\right)\left(-\frac12-1\right)\\y&=-\frac94\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$,
$$y=(0+2)(0-1)=-2.$$
The turning point is $\left(-\frac12,-\frac94\right)$ and the $y$-intercept is $(0,-2)$. The parabola opens upwards.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}-\frac12(x-2)(x-4)&=0\\x&=2\text{ or }4\end{align*}$$
The turning point is halfway between the intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{2+4}{2}\\x&=3\\y&=-\frac12(3-2)(3-4)\\y&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$,
$$y=-\frac12(0-2)(0-4)=-4.$$
The turning point is $\left(3,\frac12\right)$ and the $y$-intercept is $(0,-4)$. The parabola opens downwards.
